requirement:
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.

An anchored file or node MUST be covered by the definition's evidence under
{cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`, by an input selecting it, so changing the file makes that evidence stale. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference, because the
definition cannot be assessed without it. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.

Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file when a more precise reference is available, such
as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the
definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Every obligation has an `{impl}` site and a `{test}`, except the skills-direction obligation, which has no test (explained last).

**Parsing options (MAY, and "immediately after the opening fence, one per line").**
- `definition_blocks` and `option_line` in `src/lib.rs` read option lines directly after the fence and stop at the first non-option line.
- `Anchor::parse` in `src/evidence.rs` splits `path#selector`.
- `collect_definitions` maps `:impl:` to an Impl anchor on a `{req}`, and `:test:` to a Test anchor on a `{req}` or `{example}`.
- Test `anchor_options_are_metadata_not_body_text` (`src/lib.rs`) covers placement, only lines directly after the fence counting as options, and one option per line.

**Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge from the definition.**
- `Anchor.kind` carries the role.
- The edge feeds `AssessmentSources::prepare`, the `references` tool, the `referencing` filter, `DefinitionEdges::current` in `src/index.rs`, and `validate_references`.
- Tests: `references_report_anchors_as_file_or_node_sites`, `anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs`, the ripgrep and ast_grep referencing tests, and `detail_inputs_are_grouped_by_current_edges_in_disclosures`.

**Paths MUST follow the schema path rules.**
- `Anchor::resolve` goes through `OutlineCache::parse`, which reads the file through `read_project_file` under `requirements.ci.input_containment`.
- It rejects an empty path.
- The authoring test checks that a file under a disallowed path fails with `PermissionDenied`.

**Option lines MUST NOT be part of the definition text, requirements inputs, or rendered body.**
- `without_options` is used for `text` and `raw_lines` in `collect_definitions`, and in `preprocess_book` and `replace_definitions` for rendering.
- Tests: `requirements_inputs_omit_option_lines`, `anchor_options_are_metadata_not_body_text`, the render assertions in `every_definition_gets_a_nested_detail_page_without_an_index`, and the "text changed" check in `anchored_files_must_be_completely_covered_and_resolvable`.

**An anchored file or node MUST be covered by an input selecting it.**
- `validate_references` reports "no input selects … anchored by :impl:" unless an input selects the target node or one of its ancestors.
- `prepare` adds the anchor as a mandatory outline input.
- Tests: `anchored_files_must_be_completely_covered_and_resolvable` (including the stale-evidence check after the file changes) and `selector_anchors_are_covered_by_inputs_selecting_the_node_or_an_ancestor`.

**An unresolvable path or selector MUST be a validation error naming the definition and path, and authoring MUST report it before inference.**
- `validate_references` emits ":impl: anchor X on requirement Y … does not resolve …".
- `prepare` returns "{subject}: cannot read :impl: anchor {label}" before any inference.
- Tests: the `missing.sh` and `fn[missing]` cases in `src/evidence.rs`, and `unreadable_or_denied_anchors_fail_before_inference` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs` (missing file and disallowed path).

**Any other option line MUST be a validation error.**
- `collect_definitions` reports unsupported options, including `:impl:` on an example, and an empty value.
- Test: `unsupported_and_empty_options_are_validation_errors`.

**Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file when a more precise reference is available; the bundled skills MUST give this direction.**
- `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/references/syntax-details.md` ("Anchors") says "Don't anchor a file whose items can carry a reference themselves."
- `SKILL.md` points to that file for the cases where a file cannot carry a reference.
- The definition anchors both files with `:impl:`.
- No test checks the skill text. The skill is a static document with no conditional or transformation, so there is no code to run, and I did not count this as a gap.

text: :::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
An anchored file or node MUST be covered by the definition's evidence under
{cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`, by an input selecting it, so changing the file makes that evidence stale. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference, because the
definition cannot be assessed without it. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file when a more precise reference is available, such
as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the
definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
:::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} roles

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, and MAY use the `{fixme}` role in fenced form. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. The roles MUST mean:
- `{cite}`: the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition. It is an
edge from the source to the definition.
- `{impl}`: the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision,
performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition
specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining
one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or
producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as
implementing it. A check MUST count only if the definition states it, or the
source could not meet one of the definition's obligations without it; source
that checks it is consistent with a definition, such as recognizing a form the
definition specifies in order to decide whether to run other behavior, relies
on that definition and calls for `{cite}`. A requirement stating a convention
for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by
the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that
collects and reports those outputs.
- `{test}`: the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies:
a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome,
or a named example through the concrete case it describes.
- `{fixme}`: the source acknowledges a known gap in fulfilling the definition. It
MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST describe the gap. The body MAY
begin with option lines naming issues that track the gap, one per line, in the
form `:github: <owner>/<repo>#<number>`, such as
`:github: rust-lang/rust#123`. `github` MUST be the only recognized option.
A named `{fixme}` MAY appear only in sources outside the book. Validation MUST report
any other option line, a `:github:` value not in that form, an inline
`{fixme}`, a `{fixme}` in a requirement or example declaration, and a
`{fixme}` whose body, without option lines and comment delimiters, is empty.
An unnamed `{fixme}`, a fence of `:::{fixme}` with no name, MAY appear in any
project text, including a requirement or example body, to tie that place to
the issues it names. It MUST have at least one `:github:` option line and MAY
have a description; it is not a reference edge, acknowledges no gap, needs no
coverage, and does not count as a reference for Rust item coverage. Its
issues are checked under {cite}`requirements.cli.fixme_issues`.
`{impl}`, `{test}`, and `{fixme}` are edges from the definition to the source.
Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the
definitions it implements or tests.
```text
{impl}`requirements.references.roles`
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`
{test}`requirements.references.roles`
:::{req} schema

A requirement or example evidence file at `evidence/<full-name>.json` MUST be a JSON object with exactly `requirement` or `example`, `determination`, `rationale`, `references`, and `inputs`. `references` MUST be the reference-set digest defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`. The definition text and rationale MUST be nonempty strings, `determination` MUST use one of the outcomes defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`, and `inputs` MUST be an array. Every evidence input MUST have exactly one of three forms: an outline input with `file`, `item`, and `hash`; a requirements input with `requirements`, `matches`, and `text`; or a definition input with `definition` and `text`. File paths MUST resolve to permitted inputs under {cite}`requirements.ci.input_containment`. Project-local paths SHOULD be recorded relative to the project for portability; absolute and parent-relative paths MAY be used when their resolved targets are permitted. `matches` MUST be an array of distinct full definition names, `hash` MUST be a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, and `text` MUST be a nonempty array of strings. Evidence MUST NOT store source text for outline inputs.
:::{req} evidence_coverage

For every `{impl}` and `{test}` reference in a project source file, including one in a requirement or example declaration, and every `{fixme}` reference except one inside a site under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, the evidence file for the referenced requirement or example MUST contain an input whose resolved source ranges cover the reference's file and line. A `{cite}` reference MUST NOT require coverage; it is discoverable through {cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. Habeas MUST report every uncovered reference with its role, full name, source file, and line number.
